citations.title: Home Care Agencies and Home Care Registries
citations.requirement: Chapter 611 has General (§§611.1-611.5) and Governance and Management (§§611.51-611.57). The TOC lists no separate sections on staffing ratios, medication, or emergency preparedness.

citations.title: License required
citations.requirement: No entity may operate, maintain or hold itself out as a home care agency or registry without a Department license. Each physical location must be separately licensed.

citations.title: License required: fee, renewal and inspection
citations.requirement: $100 non-refundable application or renewal fee. Renewal form due at least 60 days before expiration. Department inspects before the initial license and before renewal.

citations.title: Affected home care agencies and home care registries
citations.requirement: Chapter 611 applies to home care agencies and home care registries (and entities meeting both definitions), for-profit or nonprofit, operated in Pennsylvania.

citations.title: Requirements for home care agencies and home care registries: copy of chapter
citations.requirement: A current copy of Chapter 611 must be maintained at the home care agency (office) at all times.

citations.title: Requirements for home care agencies and home care registries: Chapter 51 applies
citations.requirement: Chapter 51 (General Information), which applies to all licensed health care facilities, applies to licensed home care agencies and registries.

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Defines consumer, consumer control, direct care worker, direct consumer contact, companionship services (socialization, support and IADL help) and nurse (RN or LPN). Use these terms in the manual.

citations.title: Health Care Facilities Act, section 802a (definition source for IADLs)
citations.requirement: §611.5 takes 'instrumental activities of daily living' from section 802a of the Health Care Facilities Act. The IADL list defines the non-medical scope of services.

citations.title: Hiring or rostering of direct care workers: prerequisites
citations.requirement: Before hiring: hold a face-to-face interview, obtain at least 2 satisfactory (positive, verifiable, unrelated-person) references, and require a criminal history report and ChildLine verification if applicable.

citations.title: Hiring or rostering of direct care workers: direct care worker files
citations.requirement: Each worker file must document the interview date and references, plus the items required under §§611.52, 611.53 and, if applicable, §§611.54, 611.55 and 611.56.

citations.title: Criminal background checks: general rule and State Police record
citations.requirement: Each direct care worker applicant, office staff applicant and owner must obtain a criminal history report at application or within 1 year before. PA residents of 2+ years request a State Police record.

citations.title: Criminal background checks: federal record and proof of residency
citations.requirement: Non-residents of under 2 years must obtain a Federal record and a Department of Aging letter of determination. The agency may request residency proof (license, utility bill, tax return, etc.).

citations.title: Criminal background checks: prohibition
citations.requirement: May not hire, roster or retain a person whose State Police record shows a prohibited conviction under 6 Pa. Code §15.143, or whose Aging letter of determination says not eligible.

citations.title: Criminal background checks: records and confidentiality
citations.requirement: Keep criminal history records or letters for workers, office staff and owners, available for Department inspection. Keep them confidential and use them only for hire, roster or retain decisions.

citations.title: Criminal background checks: appeal notice and exceptions
citations.requirement: If a no-hire or removal decision rests on criminal records, give the person information on appealing to the record source. No new report is needed on transfer within the same owner or on change of ownership.

citations.title: Facility responsibilities (prohibited convictions list, cross-referenced by §611.52(e))
citations.requirement: Source of the prohibited-conviction list that §611.52(e) incorporates. Pull the full list from 6 Pa. Code Ch. 15 before drafting the hiring screen.

citations.title: Procedure (letter of determination, cross-referenced by §611.52(c))
citations.requirement: Procedure through which a Federal criminal history record yields a Department of Aging letter of determination for applicants not resident in PA for 2 years.

citations.title: Child abuse clearance: requirement and prohibition
citations.requirement: An agency that serves people under 18 must require a ChildLine verification from each direct care worker and office staff applicant. It may not employ or retain anyone ChildLine verifies as a perpetrator of a founded or indicated report.

citations.title: Child abuse clearance: records maintained
citations.requirement: Keep ChildLine verification copies in the file of each worker and office staff member, and for owners. These must be available for Department inspection.

citations.title: Provisional hiring: conditions
citations.requirement: Provisional hire is allowed pending reports only if the applicant applied and supplied the request forms, has no tampering disqualifier, and signs a sworn statement. Competency under §611.55 must come first, with documented random observation and consumer feedback.

citations.title: Provisional hiring: minors, time limits and termination
citations.requirement: A provisional hire awaiting child abuse clearance must be supervised or accompanied when serving a consumer under 18. Limits are 30 days (PA resident 2+ years) or 90 days. Immediate termination on disqualification or missed deadline.

citations.title: Competency requirements: routes to competency before assignment
citations.requirement: Before assignment the worker must hold a PA nurse license, pass the agency's competency exam, or complete an approved training program. Approved programs include a Medicaid waiver training program or the PDE nurse aide program.

citations.title: Competency requirements: required content
citations.requirement: Exam or training must cover confidentiality, consumer control, IADLs, changes in the consumer, infection control, universal precautions, emergencies, documentation, abuse/neglect reporting and difficult behaviors. Personal care adds bathing, toileting, transfers, meals and self-administered medication assistance.

citations.title: Competency requirements: documentation, portability and annual review
citations.requirement: File documentation of competency (and any license copy). It is transferable if the break is 12 months or less. Review competency at least once per year, and more often after discipline for a quality-of-care infraction.

citations.title: Health screening: tuberculosis before consumer contact
citations.requirement: Each direct care worker, and office staff or contractors with direct consumer contact, must document TB screening and freedom from active TB before consumer contact. Screening follows CDC guidelines and may be no more than 1 year before the start date.

citations.title: Health screening: 12-month update and file
citations.requirement: Update TB documentation at least every 12 months, counted from the last evaluation, and keep it in the individual's file.

citations.title: Consumer protections: consumer rights
citations.requirement: Consumers may take part in service planning and receive services with reasonable accommodation of needs and preferences. They get at least 10 calendar days' written notice before termination. Shorter notice applies only if the consumer is over 14 days in arrears or worker safety is at risk.

citations.title: Consumer protections: prohibitions
citations.requirement: No one affiliated with the agency may assume power of attorney or guardianship over a consumer. The agency may not require a consumer to endorse checks over to it.

citations.title: Consumer protections: information packet before services begin
citations.requirement: Before services begin, give an easy-to-read packet: services and identity of worker, hours, fees and total costs, DOH contact, DOH complaint Hot Line 1-866-826-3644 and local AAA Ombudsman number, and hiring and competency requirements.

citations.title: Consumer protections: employee/independent-contractor status disclosure
citations.requirement: The 2007 proposal (37 Pa.B. 4198) required a disclosure of the worker's employee or contractor status, with a Department-published format. Confirm in the current adopted text before relying on it.

citations.title: Consumer protections: documentation
citations.requirement: Keep on file documentation of compliance with §611.57, available for Department inspection.

citations.title: Notification: new and discontinued services
citations.requirement: Notify the Department in writing at least 60 days before starting a health care service not previously provided. Give similar 60 days' notice before ceasing an existing service. Applies via §611.4(b).

citations.title: Notification: serious noncompliance
citations.requirement: If the agency knows it is out of compliance in a way that seriously compromises quality assurance or patient safety, it must immediately notify the Department in writing, with the reason and the corrective steps.

citations.title: Notification: incident reporting
citations.requirement: Reportable events include unusual-circumstance deaths, medication-error death or serious injury, hospital transfer from injury or accident, abuse complaints, rape, disaster disruption, loss of vital utilities and unlicensed practice. Confirm the report timing in the full text.

citations.title: Change in ownership; change in management
citations.requirement: Chapter 51 has a section on change in ownership and change in management that applies via §611.4(b). Obtain the full text before drafting notice timelines.

citations.title: Identification of personnel
citations.requirement: When working in a health care facility and when clinically feasible, specified individuals must wear an identification tag. Confirm the covered personnel in the full text.

citations.title: Violations, penalties
citations.requirement: Chapter 51's sanctions provision, which applies to Chapter 611 licensees through §611.4(b).

citations.title: Mandatory reporting by facility employees and administrators
citations.requirement: An employee or administrator of a covered facility with reasonable cause to suspect abuse of a recipient must immediately make an oral report to the Area Agency on Aging. OLTL says CHC and waiver providers are mandatory reporters.

citations.title: Adult Protective Services (adults 18-59 with disabilities)
citations.requirement: Protects adults 18-59 with a disability against abuse, neglect, exploitation and abandonment, in the home or a care facility. Reports go to the statewide line, 1-800-490-8505, open 24/7.

citations.cite: PA DHS statewide abuse hotline guidance
citations.title: Report Abuse of an Adult with a Disability
citations.requirement: Suspected abuse or neglect must be reported to the hotline, 1-800-490-8505 (24/7). A call to DHS about one of the four serious allegations does not satisfy the hotline report. Free online mandated-reporter training is available.

citations.title: Critical incident and risk management
citations.requirement: OLTL HCBS providers must report critical incidents on the Department's form. They need written policies on prevention, reporting, notification, investigation and management, must give follow-up information, and must reduce preventable incidents.

citations.title: Staff training (critical incident reporting topic)
citations.requirement: OLTL HCBS provider staff training must include reporting critical incidents. Pull the full §52.21 topic and hours list before finalizing the training policy.

citations.title: Definitions (critical incident)
citations.requirement: Defines 'critical incident' for OLTL HCBS providers. The OLTL bulletin clarifies the definition, which governs what the agency must report for CHC and OBRA participants.

citations.title: Abuse
citations.requirement: OLTL HCBS abuse provision cited in the Critical Incident Management Bulletin alongside §§52.11, 52.17 and 52.21. Pull the full text before writing the abuse policy.

citations.cite: OLTL Critical Incident Management Bulletin (issued Feb. 23, 2023)
citations.title: Critical incident definitions and provider responsibilities
citations.requirement: Applies to providers in the CHC Waiver, OBRA Waiver and Act 150. The agency that discovers a critical incident submits the first section of the report within 48 hours. Providers are mandatory reporters under the APS Act and OAPSA.

citations.title: Provider notice to Service Coordinator within 24 hours
citations.requirement: Providers must inform the participant's Service Coordinator within 24 hours of discovering a critical incident. Failure can bring DHS or OLTL sanctions up to termination of the provider contract.

citations.title: Critical incident reporting and management
citations.requirement: Network providers report critical incidents to the CHC-MCO, which uses EIM. MCO notifies the participant and representative within 24 hours of the report. Providers must report even if the participant declines.

citations.cite: CHC Agreement §V.A.2, §V.J, Exhibit A(1) (missed service reporting)
citations.title: Monthly missed-service reporting for PAS
citations.requirement: Per an MCO training document, MCOs and providers must report monthly all CHC participants with a missed PAS or home health aide service. Confirm against the Agreement text and your MCO manual.

citations.cite: Medicaid EVV (21st Century Cures Act implementation in PA)
citations.title: Electronic visit verification for Medicaid personal care services
citations.requirement: Medicaid personal care visits must be captured in EVV, in effect in PA since Jan. 1, 2020. A secondary source reports an 85% verified-without-manual-edit threshold from 1/1/2025.

citations.title: Medicaid EVV requirement for personal care services
citations.requirement: Federal basis for EVV on Medicaid personal care services. Text not fetched in this session.

citations.title: Community HealthChoices waivers
citations.requirement: CHC is a capitated Medicaid managed-care program under a 1915(b) waiver (1/1/2023-12/31/2027) with a 1915(c) waiver application (Jan. 2026). Agency PAS is paid through the CHC-MCOs.

citations.title: OBRA Waiver renewal
citations.requirement: OBRA Waiver renewal approved 6/18/2026, effective 7/1/2026, expires 6/30/2031. The agency may serve OBRA participants once enrolled through OLTL.

citations.title: Home health agency licensing (separate skilled-care license)
citations.requirement: Skilled home health care needs a separate Chapter 601 license, not Chapter 611. The manual must keep caregivers within non-medical personal care and companionship.

citations.title: HIPAA Privacy, Security and Breach Notification Rules
citations.requirement: Applies if the agency is a covered entity, such as a Medicaid billing provider using standard electronic transactions. Requires privacy policies, workforce training, safeguards and breach notification. Not fetched in this session.

citations.title: OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard
citations.requirement: Employer exposure control for employees with occupational exposure to blood or OPIM. Not fetched in this session.

citations.title: FLSA application to domestic service employees (home care)
citations.requirement: Third-party home care employers owe minimum wage and overtime to caregivers, and travel and non-billable time rules apply. Not fetched in this session.

citations.title: HCBS waiver settings requirements
citations.requirement: Federal HCBS settings and person-centered planning requirements for 1915(c) waiver participants such as CHC and OBRA. Not fetched in this session.

citations.title: Nondiscrimination in federally assisted programs
citations.requirement: Medicaid-participating providers may not discriminate on the basis of race, color or national origin, including language access obligations. Not fetched in this session.

policies.category: General – §611.4 Requirements for home care agencies and home care registries
policies.title: Maintaining a Current Copy of Chapter 611 at the Agency
state_specifics: Keep a current copy of 28 Pa. Code Ch. 611 at the agency office at all times (§611.4(a)).
Chapter 611 applies to for-profit and nonprofit home care agencies and registries operating in PA (§611.3(a)). This manual models the employer-model agency.
The Administrator checks pacodeandbulletin.gov for Chapter 611 and Chapter 51 amendments at least annually and logs the review.
Keep a copy of Chapter 51 beside it, because it applies through §611.4(b).

policies.category: General – §611.4 Requirements for home care agencies and home care registries
policies.title: Compliance with Environmental, Health, Sanitation and Professional Licensure Standards; Chapter 51 General Provisions
state_specifics: Comply with applicable environmental, health, sanitation and professional licensure standards of federal, state and local authorities (§611.4(c)).
Chapter 51 (general provisions for all licensed health care facilities) applies to the agency under §611.4(b). Chapter 51 sanctions are in §51.41.
Any nurse or other licensed professional the agency uses must hold a current PA license. Unlicensed practice is a reportable event under §51.3.
Confirm municipal zoning and occupancy requirements for the office before signing a lease. No other siting rule was found.

policies.category: §611.51 Hiring or rostering of direct care workers
policies.title: Direct Care Worker Hiring Prerequisites: Interview and References
state_specifics: Hold a face-to-face interview with every direct care worker applicant before hiring or rostering.
Obtain at least 2 satisfactory references before hire. A satisfactory reference is positive and verifiable (verbal or written) from a former employer or another unrelated person.
The reference must affirm the applicant's ability to provide home care services. Relatives are not acceptable references.
Record the interview date and each reference (name, date, method, result) on the reference form.

policies.category: §611.51 Hiring or rostering of direct care workers
policies.title: Pre-Hire Clearances and Direct Care Worker File Contents
state_specifics: Before hire or roster, require a criminal history report (§611.52) and a ChildLine verification if applicable (§611.53).
Each direct care worker file must document the interview date and the references obtained.
Each file must also hold the §611.52 and §611.53 items and, if applicable, the §611.54 (provisional hire), §611.55 (competency) and §611.56 (TB) items.
Use the Direct Care Worker File Checklist. A missing item is an easy inspection citation.

policies.title: Criminal History Reports: Who Must Obtain Them, Sources and Proof of Residency
state_specifics: Each direct care worker applicant, each office staff applicant and each owner must obtain a criminal history report at application or within the preceding 1 year.
PA resident for the 2 years before the request: request a State Police criminal history record.
Not a PA resident for those 2 years: obtain a Federal criminal history record and a Department of Aging letter of determination (6 Pa. Code §15.144(b)). Allow extra lead time.

The agency may request proof of residency. Any one of these suffices: motor vehicle records; housing records; public utility records; local tax records; a signed income tax return with preprinted name and address; employment records including unemployment compensation records.
Order checks before the first day of work. Fees and who pays were not confirmed; state the agency's practice on the form.

policies.title: Prohibited Convictions: Do Not Hire, Roster or Retain
state_specifics: Do not hire, roster or retain anyone whose State Police record shows a prohibited conviction listed in 6 Pa. Code §15.143.
Do not hire, roster or retain anyone whose Department of Aging letter of determination says they are not eligible.
Pull the full §15.143 list from 6 Pa. Code Ch. 15 and attach it to the screening checklist.
On learning of a disqualifying conviction, remove the worker from consumer contact immediately and document the action.

policies.title: Criminal History Record Keeping and Confidentiality
state_specifics: Keep files for direct care workers and office staff with copies of State Police records or Department of Aging letters. Keep owners' criminal history reports too.
All of these records must be available for Department inspection.
Keep criminal history information confidential. Use it solely to decide eligibility to be hired, rostered or retained.
Store the records in a locked or access-controlled location, separate from general personnel files where practical.

policies.title: Opportunity to Appeal and Exceptions to Re-Checking
state_specifics: If a decision not to hire, roster or retain rests wholly or partly on these records, give the individual information on how to appeal to the record sources if they believe the records are in error.
No new report is required for a worker who already complied and transfers to another agency or registry owned and operated by the same entity.
No new report is required for a worker whose employer undergoes a change of ownership.
Document each exception and the basis for it in the worker's file.

policies.title: ChildLine Verification: Requirement, Prohibition and Records
state_specifics: An agency that serves persons under 18 must require each direct care worker applicant and each office staff applicant to request a ChildLine verification.
Do not employ, roster or retain anyone ChildLine verifies as the named perpetrator of a founded or indicated report of child abuse in the Statewide Central Register.
Keep ChildLine verification copies in the file of each employee, rostered individual and office staff member, and keep owners' copies. All must be available for Department inspection.
Record at intake whether the agency serves any consumer under 18. If it does, apply this policy to all applicants. If it does not, document that determination annually.

policies.title: Provisional Hiring: Eligibility Conditions
state_specifics: Provisional hire is allowed only if the applicant has applied for the criminal history report and ChildLine verification, as applicable, and has given the agency a copy of the completed request forms.
The agency must have no knowledge that would disqualify the applicant under 18 Pa.C.S. §4911.
The applicant must swear or affirm in writing that they are not disqualified under Chapter 611 (Provisional Hire Sworn Statement).
Do not assign or refer the provisional hire to any consumer until the §611.55 competency requirements are met.

policies.title: Provisional Hire Monitoring, Time Limits and Termination
state_specifics: Monitor a provisional hire awaiting a criminal background check through random direct observation and consumer feedback. Document the results in the worker's file.
A provisional hire awaiting child abuse clearance who serves a consumer under 18 must be directly supervised or accompanied by another direct care worker.
Maximum provisional period: 30 days for a PA resident of 2+ years; 90 days for anyone else. Track the end date on a tracker.
Terminate the individual or remove them from the roster immediately if the reports show disqualification, or if the report or verification is not provided within the provisional period.

policies.title: Establishing Competency Before Assignment or Referral
state_specifics: Before assigning or referring a direct care worker, confirm one route: (1) a valid PA nurse's license; (2) passing the agency's competency exam; or (3) completing an approved training program.

Approved programs: an agency or other-entity program meeting (b) and (c); a home health aide program meeting 42 CFR 484.36; the PA Department of Education nurse aide program; a Medicaid Waiver or other publicly funded HCBS program the agency participates in; or another program the Department identifies.
The 42 CFR 484.36 reference is an accepted training standard only. It does not make the agency a Medicare home health agency.
Record the route used in the worker's file.

policies.title: Competency Exam and Training Content: Core Topics for All Direct Care Workers
state_specifics: The exam or training must cover at minimum: confidentiality; consumer control and the independent living philosophy; instrumental activities of daily living (IADLs); recognizing changes in the consumer that need to be addressed.
It must also cover: basic infection control; universal precautions; handling of emergencies; documentation; recognizing and reporting abuse or neglect; dealing with difficult behaviors.
IADLs are defined by reference to section 802a of the Health Care Facilities Act (35 P.S. §448.802a).
Have a nurse or experienced administrator review the exam. Keep the exam, answer key and results.

policies.title: Competency Content for Workers Providing Personal Care
state_specifics: For workers who will provide personal care, the exam or training must also cover: bathing, shaving, grooming and dressing; hair, skin and mouth care.
It must also cover: assistance with ambulation and transferring; meal preparation and feeding; toileting; assistance with self-administered medications.
Use the Personal Care Skills Checklist with return demonstration observed by a nurse or qualified supervisor.
Do not assign personal care tasks to a worker who was cleared only for companionship or IADL tasks.

policies.title: Competency Documentation, Portability and Annual Review
state_specifics: Document each worker's satisfactory completion of competency requirements in the worker's file. Keep a copy of any nurse or other health-professional license or certification.
Documentation transfers between agencies or registries if the break in employment or roster status is 12 months or less. Verify prior records against agency standards.

Review and document competency at least once per year after initial competency. Methods: direct observation, testing, training, consumer feedback, another Department-approved method, or a combination.
Review more often when discipline or another sanction (for example a verbal warning or suspension) is imposed for a quality-of-care infraction.
Keep an annual-review due-date tracker.

policies.title: Tuberculosis Screening Before Consumer Contact and 12-Month Updates
state_specifics: Before consumer contact, each direct care worker, and any office staff or contractor with direct consumer contact, must document screening for and freedom from active mycobacterium tuberculosis.
Screening follows CDC guidelines. The documented screening date may be no more than 1 year before the start date.
Update the TB documentation at least every 12 months, counted from the last evaluation, and keep it in the individual's file.
Track expiration dates and remove from consumer contact anyone whose documentation lapses.

policies.title: Consumer Participation in Service Planning and Reasonable Accommodation
state_specifics: Consumers have the right to be involved in the service planning process.
Consumers have the right to receive services with reasonable accommodation of individual needs and preferences.
The exception is where the direct care worker's health and safety is at risk.
Document the consumer's participation and preferences in the service plan. For CHC and OBRA participants, align with person-centered planning (verify 42 CFR 441.301(c) text).

policies.title: Discharge, Transfer and Termination of Services: 10-Day Written Notice
state_specifics: Give the consumer at least 10 calendar days' advance written notice of intent to terminate services.
Shorter notice is allowed only if the consumer, despite notice, has failed to pay and is more than 14 days in arrears, or the direct care worker's health and welfare is at risk.
For Medicaid participants, also notify the Service Coordinator or MCO and help with transition to another provider.
Document the reason, the notice date and the transition steps in the client record.

policies.title: Prohibition on Power of Attorney, Guardianship and Check Endorsement
state_specifics: No one, by reason of affiliation with the agency, may assume power of attorney or guardianship over a consumer.
The agency may not require a consumer to endorse checks over to it.
Staff may not serve as a consumer's agent, representative payee or financial POA while employed by the agency.
Report any staff request or offer of such arrangements to the Administrator.

policies.title: Consumer Information Packet: Delivery, Services, Hours and Fees
state_specifics: Before services begin, give the consumer, legal representative or responsible family member an easy-to-read information packet. Obtain a signed acknowledgment.
Packet item (c)(1): a listing of the available home care services the direct care worker will provide, and the identity of the worker who will provide them.
Packet item (c)(2): the hours when services will be provided.
Packet item (c)(3): fees and total costs for the services, on an hourly or weekly basis.
Reissue the relevant pages whenever the worker, hours or fees change.

policies.title: Consumer Information Packet: Department Contacts, Complaint Line, Hiring Standards and Worker Status Disclosure
state_specifics: Packet item (c)(4): who to contact at the Department of Health for licensure requirements and for compliance information about this agency.

Packet item (c)(5): the Department's complaint Hot Line and the local Area Agency on Aging Ombudsman Program number. The official checklist lists 1-800-254-5164; the research lists 1-866-826-3644. Confirm against the current §611.57(c)(5) text before printing.
Packet item (c)(6): the hiring and competency requirements that apply to the agency's direct care workers.

Packet item (c)(7): a disclosure on the worker's employee vs. independent-contractor status and the resulting tax, insurance and other obligations. Use the format the Department published in the Pennsylvania Bulletin. This agency employs its caregivers (W-2).
Citation C30 is unverified. Confirm the adopted text and the Department's disclosure format.

policies.title: Documentation of Compliance with Consumer Protections
state_specifics: Keep documentation on file at the agency showing compliance with §611.57.
Keep it available for Department inspection.
Compliance file contents: signed packet acknowledgments, termination notices with delivery proof, and worker status disclosures.
The Administrator audits a sample of new client files quarterly.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Administrator Responsibilities
state_specifics: The owner(s) or governing body is accountable for Chapter 611 and Chapter 51 compliance and appoints an Administrator.
Administrator qualifications are unconfirmed (sources conflict). Confirm with the DOH Division of Home Health before naming one.
A new Administrator must have criminal history results no more than 1 year old (per the DOH FAQ).
Keep an organizational chart showing who is responsible for hiring files, competency, TB tracking and complaints.

policies.title: Licensure, Service Area and Advertising Requirements
state_specifics: Do not operate, maintain or hold out as a home care agency without a Department license. That includes advertising. Do not accept clients or market before the license is issued.
Each physical location needs its own license; branch offices are not recognized and a virtual office does not qualify.
The fee is $100, non-refundable and not prorated. Submit the renewal form at least 60 days before expiration. DOH inspects before the initial license and before renewal.
Apply online only (mail and email ended March 31, 2026; reconfirm payment method). Skilled nursing requires a separate Chapter 601 license.
Display the license as DOH requires and keep marketing consistent with non-medical personal care and companionship.

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
state_specifics: Review the manual at least annually and on any change to Chapter 611, Chapter 51, OLTL or MCO rules.
Version each policy and keep superseded versions.
Keep the policy manual ready for the pre-licensure and renewal inspections.
Record staff acknowledgment of revised policies.

policies.title: Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement
state_specifics: Review incidents, complaints, missed visits, EVV manual-edit rates and competency reviews at least quarterly.
Chapter 611 sets no QA committee rule. This is an operator design.
Under §51.3(e), notify the Department in writing immediately of known noncompliance that seriously compromises quality or safety, with the reason and the corrective steps.
For OLTL participants, §52.17 expects steps to reduce preventable critical incidents.

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
state_specifics: Bill Medicaid only for verified, authorized visits. Payment runs through CHC-MCOs and OLTL per contract.
Screen workers and owners against exclusion lists. Confirm list requirements with the MCOs and OLTL.
Citation C50 was not fetched; confirm text.
Do not promise Medicaid services before enrollment is complete.

policies.title: Client Rights and Responsibilities
state_specifics: Include the §611.57(a) rights (service-planning participation, 10-day notice) in the client rights statement.
Give the statement with the information packet before services begin.
Add Medicaid participant rights per the MCO or OLTL requirements.
Document that rights were explained in a language the client understands.

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
state_specifics: Tell clients how to complain to the agency, to the Department of Health complaint Hot Line (confirm the number per CP-05) and to the local Area Agency on Aging Ombudsman.
No retaliation for a complaint.
Log, investigate and resolve each complaint, and review the log for trends.
CHC participants may also use their MCO's grievance process. Confirm timelines with each MCO.

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
state_specifics: Confidentiality is a required competency topic under §611.55(b)(1).
HIPAA applies if the agency is a covered entity (for example, a Medicaid biller using standard electronic transactions). C54 was not fetched; confirm.
Designate a Privacy Officer and train staff at orientation.
Criminal history information is kept confidential under §611.52(g).

policies.title: Client Property, Gifts and Financial Exploitation Prevention
state_specifics: Staff may not take power of attorney or guardianship, and the agency may not require check endorsement (§611.57(b)).
No staff loans, gifts or access to bank cards. Set the agency's gift limit.
Suspected exploitation is reported under SAF-01.
Record any client money handled for errands with receipts.

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
state_specifics: Do not discriminate by race, color or national origin. Provide interpreter and translation help.
C58 was not fetched; confirm.
Provide reasonable accommodation for disability under the ADA.
Offer the information packet in the client's language.

policies.title: Service Agreement, Rates and Billing Disclosure
state_specifics: The agreement states services, worker, hours, and hourly or weekly fees and total costs (§611.57(c)(1)-(3)).
State the minimum hours, cancellation and billing terms, and the notice rule (10 calendar days to terminate; shorter only for >14 days in arrears or worker risk).
For Medicaid clients, state that the MCO pays the agency and the client owes no extra charge unless authorized.
Obtain the client's signature.

policies.title: Scope of Services: What Caregivers May and May Not Do
state_specifics: Services are non-medical: personal care, IADLs and companionship (as defined in §611.5).
Caregivers may assist with self-administered medications (§611.55(c)(6)). They may not perform skilled nursing tasks, which need a Chapter 601 license.
Keep a written list of tasks that are in and out of scope.
Refuse or escalate any request outside scope.

policies.title: Client Intake, Eligibility and Assessment
state_specifics: Complete intake and a needs assessment before services begin.
Verify payer and authorization. Do not start Medicaid services without a valid authorization.
Ask whether any consumer is under 18 (triggers ChildLine rules, CAC-01).
Deliver the §611.57(c) packet before the first visit.

policies.title: Service Plan and Plan Updates
state_specifics: Build the plan with the consumer's participation and preferences (§611.57(a)(1)).
For CHC and OBRA clients, follow the authorized plan from the Service Coordinator.
Update the plan on any change in condition or need.
Give the assigned worker the written task list.

policies.title: Supervision of Caregivers and Supervisory Visits
state_specifics: Chapter 611 sets no supervisor ratio. This is an operator design.
Do at least an annual direct-observation competency review (§611.55(e)).
Add more frequent observation for provisional hires (§611.54(a)(5)).
Seek consumer feedback at supervisory contacts.

policies.title: Medication Assistance and Self-Administration Support
state_specifics: Workers may assist only with self-administered medications, and must be trained (§611.55(c)(6)).
Workers may not administer medications, set doses or give injections.
Report any medication refusal, error or reaction to the supervisor and the client's prescriber or family.
A medication error causing death or serious injury is a reportable event under §51.3.

policies.title: Scheduling, Missed Visits and Continuity of Care
state_specifics: Provide the consumer's hours and worker identity before services begin (§611.57(c)(1)-(2)).
Keep a backup caregiver pool and on-call coordinator.
For CHC, MCOs expect monthly reporting of missed PAS visits (C48 unverified; confirm in the MCO manual).
Log each missed visit with the cause and the notice given.

policies.title: Electronic Visit Verification and Timekeeping
state_specifics: Medicaid personal care visits must be captured in EVV (live in PA since Jan. 1, 2020).
A secondary source reports an 85% verified-without-manual-edit threshold with quarterly alerts from January 2026. Confirm with the MCO.
CHC plans use HHAeXchange per the vendor's site.
Review manual-edit rates monthly and retrain workers with frequent edits.

policies.title: Change in Client Condition and Emergencies in the Home
state_specifics: Recognizing changes in the consumer and handling emergencies are required competency topics (§611.55(b)(4), (b)(7)).
Call 911 first for emergencies, then the supervisor.
A hospital transfer from injury or accident is a reportable event under §51.3.
For OLTL participants, report critical incidents (see SAF-02).

policies.title: Coordination with Medicaid Programs and Payers
state_specifics: Licensure comes first; the OLTL waiver application follows. Agency PAS under CHC is paid through the MCOs.
The OBRA Waiver was renewed effective 7/1/2026 through 6/30/2031.
Notify the participant's Service Coordinator within 24 hours of a critical incident.
Ask each CHC-MCO about credentialing and rates (HCPCS W1793). Network status is unverified.

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Staff are mandatory reporters. OAPSA requires an immediate oral report to the Area Agency on Aging when there is reasonable cause to suspect abuse of an older adult.
For adults 18-59 with a disability (APS Act), call 1-800-490-8505 (24/7). A call to DHS about one of the four serious allegations does not satisfy the hotline report.
Reporting abuse or neglect is a required competency topic (§611.55(b)(9)).
Child abuse: report under the Child Protective Services Law (confirm the ChildLine number).
Never retaliate against a reporter.

policies.title: Incident Reporting
state_specifics: For CHC, OBRA and Act 150 participants, the agency that discovers a critical incident submits the first section of the report within 48 hours.
Inform the Service Coordinator within 24 hours. Report to the CHC-MCO (EIM) even if the participant declines.

§51.3 reportable events include unusual-circumstance deaths, medication-error death or serious injury, hospital transfer from injury or accident, abuse complaints, rape, disaster disruption and loss of vital utilities. Confirm report timing in the full §51.3 text.
Train staff on critical incident reporting (§52.21).

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
state_specifics: Basic infection control and universal precautions are required competency topics (§611.55(b)(5)-(6)).
Maintain an OSHA exposure control plan and PPE supply. C55 was not fetched; confirm.
Workers with TB symptoms or exposure leave consumer contact until cleared (§611.56).
Provide supplies and hand-hygiene training.

policies.title: Client Emergency and Disaster Plans
state_specifics: Chapter 611 has no separate emergency preparedness section. This is an operator design.
Rank clients by risk. Keep an emergency contact list.
Disaster disruption and loss of utilities are reportable under §51.3.
Test the call-tree annually.

policies.title: Caregiver Safety in the Home and Workplace Violence
state_specifics: §611.57(a) permits limiting accommodations or giving shorter termination notice where a worker's health, safety or welfare is at risk.
Allow workers to leave an unsafe setting and report it.
Do a home safety check at intake.
Provide training on safe transfers and difficult behaviors (§611.55(b)(10)).

policies.title: Transporting Clients
state_specifics: Chapter 611 sets no transport rule. This is an operator design.
Require a valid license and insurance. Carry hired and non-owned auto coverage.
Transport only if the service plan authorizes it.
Report any crash as an incident (SAF-02).

policies.title: Caregiver Qualifications and Employment Classification
state_specifics: Direct care workers are W-2 employees of the agency.
Pennsylvania has no separate registry for home care aides. Qualification rests on §611.51-.56.
Competency is required before any assignment (§611.55).
Disclose employee status in the client packet.

policies.title: Orientation, Competency Evaluation and Annual Training
state_specifics: Cover all §611.55(b) and (c) topics at orientation.
Add HIPAA, bloodborne pathogens, abuse reporting and critical incident reporting.
Chapter 611 sets no training-hour minimum (unverified); confirm with DOH.
Review competency at least annually (§611.55(e)).

policies.title: Personnel Records
state_specifics: Direct care worker files follow §611.51(b).
Office staff files need criminal history, ChildLine (where applicable) and TB (if direct contact) records.
Owners' reports are kept as well.
Confirm retention periods against Chapter 51 and Chapter 611.

policies.title: Wage, Hour and Overtime Compliance
state_specifics: Pay at least the PA minimum wage ($7.25/hr in 2026).
Third-party employers owe overtime to home care workers (C56 not fetched; confirm).
Pay travel between clients and training time as required.
Use a payroll service and review with an employment attorney.

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: No gifts, loans or financial dealings with clients (see CR-04).
No POA or guardianship (§611.57(b)).
Maintain confidentiality.
Discipline for quality-of-care infractions triggers an extra competency review (§611.55(e)).

policies.title: Client Records and Retention
state_specifics: Keep packet acknowledgments, plans, visit notes and termination notices.
Keep them available for Department inspection.
Retention period: confirm in Chapter 51 or Chapter 611 and OLTL or MCO contracts.
Use locked or access-controlled storage.

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
state_specifics: Give the Department 60 days' written notice before starting a new service or ceasing an existing one (§51.3).
Give immediate written notice of serious noncompliance (§51.3(e)).
A change of ownership of 5% or more needs approval before it occurs (§51.4).
Submit the renewal at least 60 days before expiration with the $100 fee.

documents.title: 28 Pa. Code Chapter 611 – Home Care Agencies and Home Care Registries (DOH-hosted PDF of the regulation, §§611.1–611.57)
documents.form_number: 28 Pa. Code Ch. 611 (Subpart H); no separate form number
documents.issuer: PA Department of Health, Bureau of Health Care Facilities and Home Care Services – Division of Home Health
documents.version: DOH PDF text (adopted Dec. 12, 2009; includes 611.1–611.57). The PDF does not show an amendment date. The brief reports the Pa. Code as current through 56 Pa.B. 4026 (July 4, 2026); I could not fetch the Pa. Code site to check that.
documents.how_used: No single official policy-review checklist was retrievable. The fetched PDF is the regulation itself, so required_items come from the Chapter 611 sections that set written-policy, procedure and training content (§§611.4, 611.51–611.57). Application-only items in §611.2 are excluded (form, $100 fee, separate application per location).

documents.title: Home Care Agency/Registry Change of Ownership or Control packet (contains the 'Attestation of Policies and Procedures Compliance' form)
documents.issuer: PA Department of Health, Division of Home Health
documents.version: Undated in the search snippet; the full document could not be fetched.
documents.how_used: Shows that DOH requires a signed attestation that the entity's policies and procedures are defined in its named manual(s) and comply with State/Federal requirements. This is a submission requirement, not a content list. I only saw search-result text for this form, so confirm the current wording.

documents.title: Initial Home Care Agency/Registry Application with Licensure Application Checklist (not fetched from an official URL)
documents.issuer: PA Department of Health, Division of Home Health
documents.version: A search result describes a version 'Revised January 14, 2021' with a checklist that must be submitted. DOH has since reportedly moved to an online portal (paper/email stopped Mar. 31, 2026), but that is from secondary sources only.
documents.how_used: Not used for required_items. The DOH home care page loaded, but its content was cut off before any application links, and I could not fetch the official application PDF. The checklist exists and lists a 'required policies' item with labeled exhibits, but I could not retrieve its exhibit list from an official source, so I list none.

required_items.text: A current copy of Chapter 611 must be maintained at the home care agency or registry.

Comply with applicable environmental, health, sanitation and professional licensure standards required by Federal, State and local authorities. Chapter 51 (general health-facility provisions) also applies under §611.4(b).
Before hiring or rostering a direct care worker: conduct a face-to-face interview with the individual.

Before hiring or rostering: obtain at least two satisfactory references. A satisfactory reference is positive and verifiable (verbal or written) from a former employer or other unrelated person who affirms the individual's ability to provide home care services.
Before hiring or rostering: require the individual to submit a criminal history report (per §611.52) and a ChildLine verification, if applicable (per §611.53).

Direct care worker files must document the date of the face-to-face interview and the references obtained. They must also hold the information required by §§611.52 and 611.53 and, if applicable, §§611.54, 611.55 and 611.56.
Require each direct care worker applicant to submit a criminal history report obtained at application or within the preceding 1 year. Office staff applicants and the owner(s) must also obtain one.
If the individual has been a PA resident for the 2 years before the request, they must request a State Police criminal history record.
If not a PA resident for those 2 years, the individual must obtain a Federal criminal history record and a Department of Aging letter of determination (per 6 Pa. Code §15.144(b)).

The agency or registry may request proof of residency, shown by any one of these: motor vehicle records; housing records; public utility records; local tax records; a signed income tax return with preprinted name and address; or employment records, including unemployment compensation records.

Prohibition: do not hire, roster or retain an individual if the State Police record shows a prohibited conviction listed in 6 Pa. Code §15.143, or if the Department of Aging letter says the individual is not eligible for hire or roster.

Records: keep files for direct care workers and office staff with copies of State Police records or Department of Aging letters, and keep owners' criminal history reports. All must be available for Department inspection.
Confidentiality: keep criminal history information confidential and use it solely to decide eligibility to be hired, rostered or retained.

Opportunity to appeal: if a decision not to hire, roster or retain rests wholly or partly on these records, give the individual information on how to appeal to the record sources if they believe the records are in error.

Exceptions: no new report is required for a worker who has complied and transfers to another agency or registry owned and operated by the same entity, or whose employer undergoes a change of ownership.
An agency or registry that serves persons under 18 must require each direct care worker applicant and each office staff applicant to request a ChildLine verification.
Prohibition: do not employ, roster or retain an individual whom ChildLine verifies as named in the Statewide Central Register as the perpetrator of a founded or indicated report of child abuse.
Records: keep ChildLine verification copies in the file of each employee, rostered individual and office staff member, and keep owners' copies. All must be available for Department inspection.

Provisional hiring is permitted only if the applicant has applied for a criminal history report and ChildLine verification, as applicable, and has given the agency or registry a copy of the completed request forms.
The agency or registry has no knowledge that would disqualify the applicant under 18 Pa.C.S. §4911.
The applicant swears or affirms in writing that they are not disqualified under Chapter 611.
Do not assign or refer the provisional hire until the §611.55 competency requirements are met.
Monitor the provisional hire awaiting a criminal background check through random direct observation and consumer feedback, and document the results in the individual's file.
Directly supervise, or assign another direct care worker to accompany, a provisional hire awaiting child abuse clearance who will serve a consumer under 18.
Provisional hire may not exceed 30 days for an individual who has been a PA resident for 2+ years, or 90 days for one who has not.

Termination: if the reports show disqualification, or the individual fails to provide the ChildLine verification or criminal history report within the provisional period, terminate the individual or remove them from the roster immediately.

Before assigning or referring a direct care worker, ensure the worker has either: (1) a valid PA nurse's license; (2) passed an agency/registry-developed competency examination meeting (b) and (c); or (3) completed one of these: (i) an agency/registry or other-entity training program meeting (b) and (c); (ii) a home health aide program meeting 42 CFR 484.36; (iii) the Department of Education nurse aide certification and training program; (iv) a training program meeting the standards of a Medicaid Waiver or other publicly funded HCBS program the agency participates in; (v) another program the Department identifies.
Competency exam/training must address at minimum: Confidentiality.
Consumer control and the independent living philosophy.
Instrumental activities of daily living.
Recognizing changes in the consumer that need to be addressed.
Basic infection control.
Universal precautions.
Handling of emergencies.
Documentation.
Recognizing and reporting abuse or neglect.
Dealing with difficult behaviors.
For direct care workers who will provide personal care, the exam/training must also address: Bathing, shaving, grooming and dressing.
Hair, skin and mouth care.
Assistance with ambulation and transferring.
Meal preparation and feeding.
Toileting.
Assistance with self-administered medications.

Document each worker's satisfactory completion of competency requirements in the worker's file. Keep a copy of any nurse or other health-professional license or certification. Documentation transfers between agencies/registries if the break in employment or roster status does not exceed 12 months.

Document in the worker's file a review of competency to perform assigned duties (direct observation, testing, training, consumer feedback, other Department-approved method, or a combination). Do it at least once per year after initial competency, and more often when discipline or other sanction (e.g., verbal warning or suspension) is imposed for a quality-of-care infraction.

Before consumer contact, each direct care worker and any other office staff or contractor with direct consumer contact must provide documentation of screening for, and freedom from, active mycobacterium tuberculosis. Screening follows CDC guidelines, and the documented screening date may not be more than 1 year before the start date.
Require those individuals to update the TB documentation at least every 12 months (counted from the last evaluation) and keep it in the individual's file.

Consumer right: to be involved in the service planning process and to receive services with reasonable accommodation of individual needs and preferences, except where the direct care worker's health and safety is at risk.

Consumer right: to receive at least 10 calendar days' advance written notice of intent to terminate services. Shorter notice is allowed if the consumer, despite notice, has failed to pay and is more than 14 days in arrears, or if the direct care worker's health and welfare is at risk.

Prohibitions: no one, by reason of their affiliation with the agency or registry, may assume power of attorney or guardianship over a consumer. The agency or registry may not require a consumer to endorse checks over to it.
Before services begin, give the consumer, legal representative or responsible family member an easy-to-read information packet containing items (c)(1)–(c)(7) below.
Packet item: a listing of the available home care services that will be provided by the direct care worker, and the identity of the worker who will provide them.
Packet item: the hours when services will be provided.
Packet item: fees and total costs for the services on an hourly or weekly basis.
Packet item: who to contact at the Department for information about licensure requirements and for compliance information about the particular agency or registry.
Packet item: the Department's complaint Hot Line (1-800-254-5164) and the telephone number of the local Area Agency on Aging Ombudsman Program.
Packet item: the hiring and competency requirements applicable to direct care workers employed by the agency or referred by the registry.

Packet item: a disclosure, in the format published by the Department in the Pennsylvania Bulletin, on the worker's employee vs. independent-contractor status and the resulting tax, insurance and other obligations of the consumer and the agency or registry.
Keep documentation on file at the agency or registry showing compliance with §611.57, available for Department inspection.

official.notes:
1) No single official 'policy checklist' was retrievable. Chapter 611 has no plan-of-operation or written-policy-list section. Its operational content is §§611.51–611.57 (the 'Governance and Management' subchapter), which is why the items above follow those sections. Chapter 51 also applies under §611.4(b), but I did not fetch it, so its policy requirements are not listed.
2) How DOH expects submission: licensure is by application to the Division of Home Health with a $100 fee per location (§611.2). DOH inspects before an initial license and before renewal (§611.2(a)). A copy of Chapter 611 must be kept on site (§611.4(a)). The change-of-ownership packet requires a signed 'Attestation of Policies and Procedures Compliance' naming the manual(s) that define the entity's policies.
3) Unverified, from secondary sources only: DOH takes applications online only since Mar. 31, 2026. The Jan. 14, 2021 application packet says to label exhibits, submit a checklist, and include 'required policies'. That packet says deficient applications get 30 days to resubmit revised policies. Third-party consultants organize manuals as exhibits tracking §§611.51–611.57. This is not an official format, so use the section order above, number each policy to the cited section (e.g., 611.52(h)), and confirm the current application and checklist with DOH (ra-dhhomehealth@pa.gov).
4) Medicaid PAS (CHC/OBRA Waiver) enrollment is outside Chapter 611, and I did not review it. Those programs may require additional written policies (e.g., incident reporting, EVV, abuse/neglect). Do not treat this list as complete for Medicaid participation.
5) The 'text' fields are condensed paraphrases of the regulation, not verbatim quotations. The item_id and cite values follow the document's own numbering.
